name: 魚・創作料理 花しば (Uo Sosaku Ryori Hanashiba)

claims.text: Sashimi and grilled-fish dishes are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no gluten-free soy sauce or accommodation is documented.
Hot pots and the kitchen broadly rely on fish dashi; the menu is fish-centric with no documented plant-based options.

name: 茶・アートカフェ うつぎ (Utsugi (Cha Art Cafe Utsugi))

claims.text: The menu is built around brewed Nara teas, which are naturally gluten-free and vegan; pairing sweets can be discussed item by item with the host.

name: わんずはーと・かふぇ ならまち店 (Wanzu Heart Cafe Naramachi-ten)

claims.text: An official Nara tourism listing publishes an allergen note for the signature lunch, indicating the kitchen is aware of allergens (it lists shrimp, wheat and eggs).
The hotel provides an allergen-information document, indicating that allergy inquiries are handled, though specific gluten/vegan handling details were not published.

name: 和食cafe&bar Comfy (Washoku cafe & bar Comfy)

claims.text: Cooking is built on freshly drawn Japanese dashi and locally made soy sauce and miso, so wheat-derived soy sauce and shared preparation make cross-contact likely; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The kitchen uses Inoue Honten soy sauce and miso (standard Japanese soy sauce, which normally contains wheat); no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.

Dashi is drawn fresh each morning (fish-based) and set meals include fish, chicken, dairy and eggs, so vegetable side dishes are very likely cooked with fish stock and soy sauce; no vegan preparation is documented.
Vegetables are sourced directly from farmers in Gojo City and a generous set includes around ten vegetable side dishes, so vegetable-forward eating is possible even if not certified vegan.

name: 和食とお酒 やまと庵 近鉄奈良駅前店 (Washoku to Osake Yamatoan Kintetsu Nara Ekim)

claims.text: Menu features wheat-based Miwa sōmen and tempura plus soy-sauce-seasoned dishes; no gluten-free handling or cross-contamination controls are documented.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (wheat-containing) is used throughout, including with persimmon-leaf sushi and grilled/braised dishes.
Kitchen centers on meat, game, and seafood with fish-based dashi; shared preparation makes incidental animal-product contact likely for any vegetable dish.

name: やちむんカフェ おことパーラー (Yachimun Cafe Okoto Parlour)

claims.text: Menu includes wheat-based cakes and tarts, and shaved ice is topped with Okinawan senbei crackers (wheat); no allergen labeling or gluten-free handling is described.
Signature desserts use dairy custard, cheese/tiramisu elements and cakes; most items are not dairy-free and there is no documented vegan preparation.
Some plant-based Okinawan ingredients feature on the menu, including island-tofu-based sweets, purple sweet potato (ta'amu), fuuchiba (mugwort) and fresh fruit.

name: 大和茶カフェ 茶樂茶 (Yamato-cha Cafe Sarasa)

claims.text: The house specialty is brewed Yamato tea, which is naturally plant-based and gluten-free, so a tea-only order is the safest choice for restricted diets.
